findings.claim: The constrained delay-history control supplies a reproducible5ms native-voltage predictor across held acquisition traces.
findings.known_prior_art: Autoregressive waveform prediction is established and is not a physical-law discovery.
findings.falsification: No independent object, unknown excitation mapping and unresolved voltage-to-velocity calibration.

findings.claim: Enforcing DC-offset invariance materially improves the harmonic predictor and removes much of its systematic bias.
findings.known_prior_art: A harmonic-plus-constant recurrence is a known signal-processing identity; empirical transfer is the tested result.
findings.falsification: Flexiblecontrol remains better; no claim that the object is an exact linear oscillator.
findings.scope: Initialwindowcentering can retain phase-dependent DC error.

findings.claim: The tested cubic-restoring, quadratic-drag and common-drive closures do not establish a superior physical model from these raw voltage traces.
findings.equation: Mechanistic-inspired delay closures are fully specified in rules.json.
findings.evidence: All lose to the matched flexible control in development and confirmation.
findings.known_prior_art: The sourcepaper already reports SINDy nonlinearities on converted/filtered time series; that is a different information/processing contract.
findings.falsification: Our result does not refute the sourcepaper’s fullmechanicalanalysis.

scientific_adjudication: Agent-assisted analysis; not independent experimental replication or human expert adjudication.
